children.title: Lyapunov Stability Certificates
children.top_down_role: Energy-based structures used to establish stochastic stability.

knowledge_statements.title: Lyapunov Stability Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A discrete conditional-drift certificate for almost-sure boundedness of stochastic-approximation iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_n,\mathcal F_n)\) be adapted and let \(V:\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)\) be coercive. Suppose predictable sequences \(a_n,b_n\geq0\) and a measurable \(W\geq0\) satisfy \(\sum_n b_n<\infty\) almost surely and \[\mathbb E[V(x_{n+1})\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq V(x_n)-a_nW(x_n)+b_n.\] Then the almost-supermartingale conclusion gives finite almost-sure convergence of \(V(x_n)\) and \(\sum_n a_nW(x_n)<\infty\). Consequently \(\sup_nV(x_n)<\infty\), and coercivity certifies \(\sup_n\lVert x_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive nonnegative Lyapunov function with summably perturbed negative conditional drift certifies bounded iterates and finite accumulated dissipation almost surely.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional-drift inequality holds almost surely for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x_n)\) converges finitely, \(\sum_n a_nW(x_n)<\infty\), and \(\sup_n\lVert x_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits, but an authoritative almost-supermartingale source is required to verify the necessary integrability and measurability hypotheses for the asserted convergence and dissipation conclusions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stochastic Pseudogradient Lyapunov Assumptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumption package for a stochastic iteration with Lyapunov function \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the direction process is Markov in the sense that the distribution of \(s^k\) depends only on \((x^k,k)\), with the stated independence across the direction variables; \(V\ge0\), \(\inf_xV(x)=0\), and \(V\) is differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient; \(\langle\nabla V(x^k),\mathbf E[s^k\mid x^k]\rangle\ge0\); \(\mathbf E[\|s^k\|^2\mid x^k]\le\sigma^2+\tau\langle\nabla V(x^k),\mathbf E[s^k\mid x^k]\rangle\); \(\mathbf E V(x^0)<\infty\); and \(\gamma_k\ge0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k=\infty\), with \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\gamma_k<2/(L\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stochastic process is assumed Markov with the stated independence, driven by mean pseudogradient directions for a nonnegative smooth Lyapunov function. Its conditional second moment is bounded by additive noise plus a multiple of the mean Lyapunov descent, the initial Lyapunov value is integrable, and the nonnegative step sizes have divergent sum and an asymptotic value below 2/(L tau).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stochastic iteration satisfies the basic pseudogradient--Lyapunov conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robbins–Siegmund Almost-Supermartingale Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A stochastic Lyapunov-drift convergence lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_k,u_k,\alpha_k,\beta_k\ge 0\) be random variables adapted to histories \(\mathcal F_k\). If \(\mathbf E[v_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le(1+\alpha_k)v_k-u_k+\beta_k\) almost surely and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k<\infty\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\beta_k<\infty\) almost surely, then \(v_k\to v\) almost surely for some finite random variable \(v\ge0\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}u_k<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a nonnegative adapted process has an almost-supermartingale drift inequality whose multiplicative and additive errors are summable almost surely, then the process converges almost surely to a finite nonnegative random variable and its nonnegative descent terms are summable almost surely.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure convergence and a tail-probability bound under strong pseudogradience.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose conditions (a)--(f) and the strong pseudogradient condition hold. If either \(\sigma^2=0\) or \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k^2<\infty\), then for every admissible initial point, \(V(x^k)\to0\) almost surely. Moreover, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) and every \(k\), \[\mathbf P\!\left(V(x^i)\le\varepsilon\ \forall i\ge k\right)\ge1-\varepsilon^{-1}\left(\mathbf E V(x^k)+\frac12L\sigma^2\sum_{i=k}^{\infty}\gamma_i^2\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the basic stochastic Lyapunov assumptions and strong pseudogradience, absence of additive noise or square-summability of the step sizes forces the Lyapunov values to converge almost surely to zero. A quantitative lower bound controls the probability that all values after a given index remain below a prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \text{Conditions (a)--(f) and the strong pseudogradient condition hold.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lyapunov Descent-or-Return Inductive Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inductive stability step for excursions between stopping indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m>M\) and \(n_0(\omega)\ge N(\omega,m)\). If \(n_i(\omega)<\infty\) and \(y_{n_i}(\omega)\in H^m\), then almost surely: (i) \(y_j(\omega)\in N^{\delta_m}(H^m)\) for every \(n_i(\omega)\le j\le n_{i+1}(\omega)\); (ii) \(n_{i+1}(\omega)<\infty\); and (iii) either \[V(y_{n_{i+1}}(\omega))<V(y_{n_i}(\omega))-\frac{\epsilon_m}{2},\] or \(y_{n_{i+1}}(\omega)\in N^{\delta_m}(H^M)\). In either case, \(y_{n_{i+1}}(\omega)\in H^m\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting sufficiently late, an excursion begun in H superscript m remains in its delta-m neighborhood until the next stopping index, that index is finite, and the endpoint either decreases the Lyapunov value by more than epsilon-m over two or enters the delta-m neighborhood of H superscript M. The endpoint consequently remains in H superscript m.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}y_j(\omega)\in N^{\delta_m}(H^m)\quad(n_i(\omega)\le j\le n_{i+1}(\omega)),\\ n_{i+1}(\omega)<\infty,\\ V(y_{n_{i+1}}(\omega))<V(y_{n_i}(\omega))-\epsilon_m/2\ \ \text{or}\ \ y_{n_{i+1}}(\omega)\in N^{\delta_m}(H^M),\\ y_{n_{i+1}}(\omega)\in H^m\end{gathered}\quad\text{a.s.}

children.title: Negative-Drift Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regions where expected motion favors lower Lyapunov levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Drift Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional Lyapunov drift outside a stability region, allowing summable perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an adapted recursion \((x_n,\mathcal F_n)\), a Lyapunov function \(V\geq0\), a measurable dissipation function \(W\geq0\), and a measurable stability region \(K\), a negative-drift regime holds when predictable \(a_n,b_n\geq0\) satisfy \[\mathbb E[V(x_{n+1})-V(x_n)\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq-a_nW(x_n)\mathbf 1_{\{x_n\notin K\}}+b_n\] almost surely, with \(\sum_n b_n<\infty\). A strict regime additionally requires \(\inf_{x\notin K}W(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside a designated stability region, expected Lyapunov change is negative up to a summable error; strict drift has uniformly positive dissipation there.
assumptions_latex: \((x_n,\mathcal F_n)\) is adapted and \(V,W\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality defines a negative-drift regime; it is strict if \(\inf_{x\notin K}W(x)>0\).

notation.meaning: region inside which strict drift need not hold

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the negative-drift leaf, but the exact predictable, summable-remainder, and strict-dissipation formulation has no cited source.

children.title: Coercive Stability Geometry
children.top_down_role: Large-scale energy geometry supporting bounded stochastic trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Stability Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-sublevel geometry converting a Lyapunov bound into an iterate bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V:\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)\) be lower semicontinuous and coercive, meaning \(V(x)\to\infty\) whenever \(\lVert x\rVert\to\infty\). Then every sublevel set \(L_c=\{x:V(x)\leq c\}\) is compact. Hence, on any sample path for which \(\sup_nV(x_n)=c<\infty\), all iterates belong to the compact set \(L_c\), so \(\sup_n\lVert x_n\rVert<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-semicontinuous coercive Lyapunov function has compact sublevels, so bounded Lyapunov values force bounded iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(c<\infty\), \(L_c\) is compact, and \(\sup_nV(x_n)<\infty\) implies \(\sup_n\lVert x_n\rVert<\infty\).

notation.meaning: c-sublevel set of the Lyapunov function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is mathematically standard and matches the leaf, but standard-field rationale does not replace the required inspectable citation and locator.

children.title: Drift-Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regions where stabilizing drift becomes too weak or changes direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Drift-Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-walk counterexample showing that nonnegative Lyapunov drift does not certify boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0=0\) and \(x_{n+1}=x_n+\xi_{n+1}\), where \((\xi_n)\) are independent with \(\mathbb P(\xi_n=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_n=-1)=1/2\), and take \(V(x)=x^2\). Then \[\mathbb E[V(x_{n+1})-V(x_n)\mid\mathcal F_n]=1.\] Thus no negative-drift inequality with summable positive remainder can hold outside a compact set for this \(V\). The one-dimensional simple symmetric random walk is almost surely unbounded, so coercivity of \(V\) alone does not supply a stability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric random walk has coercive quadratic Lyapunov function but positive unit drift and is almost surely unbounded, exposing the boundary of drift-based stability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample fits the failure-boundary leaf and its drift computation is coherent, but the almost-sure unboundedness claim and resulting impossibility statement require a source.

children.title: Explicit Recursion Stabilization Family

children.title: Projected Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Iterate control through restriction to a prescribed feasible region.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection stabilizes stochastic approximation within a prescribed closed convex region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), initialize \(x_0\in C\). For \(n\geq0\), obtain a stochastic direction \(G_n\), choose a gain \(a_n>0\), and update \[x_{n+1}=\Pi_C(x_n-a_nG_n),\qquad \Pi_C(y)=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{z\in C}\lVert z-y\rVert.\] Stop according to a prescribed iteration or accuracy rule and output the final iterate or a specified average. The projection guarantees \(x_n\in C\) for every \(n\), and therefore boundedness whenever \(C\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project every stochastic update onto a closed convex region; feasibility is invariant, and a bounded region directly stabilizes all iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n\in C\) for all \(n\); if \(C\) is bounded, then \(\sup_n\lVert x_n\rVert<\infty\).

children.title: Truncated Recursions
children.top_down_role: Recursion control through rejection, clipping, or reset mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Recursions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reset-based truncation prevents accepted stochastic-approximation iterates from leaving prescribed regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((K_j)_{j\geq0}\) be closed truncation regions, let \(r_j\in K_j\) be reset points, and initialize \(x_0\in K_0\), \(\sigma_0=0\). At iteration \(n\), form \(y_{n+1}=x_n+a_nH(x_n,\xi_{n+1})\). If \(y_{n+1}\in K_{\sigma_n}\), set \((x_{n+1},\sigma_{n+1})=(y_{n+1},\sigma_n)\); otherwise set \((x_{n+1},\sigma_{n+1})=(r_{\sigma_n+1},\sigma_n+1)\). After the stopping index, output \(x_n\) together with the truncation count \(\sigma_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a proposed stochastic-approximation step inside the active region; otherwise reset to a safe point and advance the truncation index.
assumptions_latex: \(K_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is closed and \(r_j\in K_j\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate lies in its active region, while \(\sigma_n\) records the number of rejected proposals.

notation.meaning: safe reset point for region j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reset-based algorithm fits the leaf, but no citation establishes this exact truncation-index and reset-point convention.

children.title: Expanding-Region Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Iterate control through a sequence of progressively larger regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Expanding-Region Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncation with nested regions whose union covers the state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose compact sets \(K_0\subseteq K_1\subseteq\cdots\) with \(K_j\subseteq\operatorname{int}K_{j+1}\) and \(\bigcup_{j\geq0}K_j=\mathbb{R}^d\), together with reset points \(r_j\in K_j\). Initialize \((x_0,\sigma_0)=(r_0,0)\). Given \(y_{n+1}=x_n+a_nH(x_n,\xi_{n+1})\), accept it without changing \(\sigma_n\) when \(y_{n+1}\in K_{\sigma_n}\); otherwise set \(x_{n+1}=r_{\sigma_n+1}\) and \(\sigma_{n+1}=\sigma_n+1\). Output the terminal iterate and truncation count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use nested compact acceptance regions; each rejected proposal triggers a reset and enlarges the active region, eventually admitting every fixed bounded subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every bounded \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), there exists \(j_B\) such that \(B\subseteq K_j\) for all \(j\geq j_B\).

notation.meaning: reset point in the j-th region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expanding-region algorithm and exhaustion conclusion are coherent, but the specific nested-region truncation scheme lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Stabilization-Induced Bias
children.top_down_role: Target distortion introduced by active iterate-control mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Induced Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-mean bias introduced by projecting or truncating an otherwise unbiased stochastic update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the unstabilized proposal be \(y_{n+1}=x_n-a_nG_n\), where \(\mathbb E[G_n\mid\mathcal F_n]=g(x_n)\), and let a measurable stabilizer \(S_n\) produce \(x_{n+1}=S_n(y_{n+1})\). Define \[b_n^{\mathrm{stab}}=a_n^{-1}\mathbb E[S_n(y_{n+1})-y_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n].\] Then the stabilized conditional mean increment has the exact representation \[\mathbb E[x_{n+1}-x_n\mid\mathcal F_n]=-a_ng(x_n)+a_nb_n^{\mathrm{stab}}.\] Thus stabilization is conditionally unbiased precisely when \(b_n^{\mathrm{stab}}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional mean correction caused by projection, truncation, or resetting is an additive drift bias equal to the expected stabilization displacement divided by the gain.
assumptions_latex: \(a_n>0\), and \(x_n,G_n\) are integrable as required by the displayed expectations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[x_{n+1}-x_n\mid\mathcal F_n]=-a_ng(x_n)+a_nb_n^{\mathrm{stab}}\), with zero stabilization bias exactly when \(b_n^{\mathrm{stab}}=0\).

notation.meaning: conditional drift bias induced by stabilization
conditional mean of the unstabilized direction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact conditional-mean decomposition fits the stabilization-bias leaf, but no source supports this definition and its interpretation for projection, truncation, and resetting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-horizon scaled-flow comparison bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Gronwall-type comparison estimate under the standing scaled-drift and Lipschitz hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be compact and let \(T>0\). Under the standing scaled-flow hypotheses, there is a quantity \(\epsilon(c)\), independent of \(x_0\in K\), such that \(\epsilon(c)\to0\) as \(c\to\infty\) and, for \(t\in[0,T]\), \(x_0\in K\), and each admissible initial condition \(x\), \[\|\phi_c(t,x)-\phi_\infty(t,x_0)\|\leq\bigl(\|x-x_0\|+\epsilon(c)T\bigr)e^{LT}.\] In particular, when \(x=x_0\), \[\|\phi_c(t,x_0)-\phi_\infty(t,x_0)\|\leq\epsilon(c)Te^{LT}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed finite time interval and compact set of reference initial conditions, the scaled and limiting flows differ by the initial discrepancy plus an error that tends uniformly to zero as the scale grows.
assumptions_latex: \phi_c\text{ and }\phi_\infty\text{ satisfy the standing scaled-flow hypotheses}
L\text{ is the Lipschitz constant appearing in those hypotheses}
x\text{ is an admissible initial condition for }\phi_c

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Observation-truncated robust stochastic approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustification caps the influence of individual observations; it may be combined with iterate projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For i=1,\ldots,r, let \psi_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R be bounded, monotonically nondecreasing, odd, satisfy \psi_i(0)=0, and obey \psi_i(u)/u\to0 as u\to\infty. With \psi(y)=(\psi_1(y^1),\ldots,\psi_r(y^r)), the robust recursion is \[\theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+\epsilon_n\psi(Y_n).\] Because each \psi_i is bounded, a single arbitrarily large observation cannot produce an arbitrarily large normalized update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a bounded, monotone, odd transformation componentwise to each observation before updating. This limits the effect of extreme observation noise; clipping at fixed thresholds is a standard instance.
assumptions_latex: \psi_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\text{ is bounded and monotonically nondecreasing}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability theorem establishing repeated returns, return-to-return excursion control, and boundedness in probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume recursion (7.1). Let \(V\) have continuous first and bounded mixed second partial derivatives, satisfy \(V(0)=0\), and obey \(V(\theta)\to\infty\) as \(|\theta|\to\infty\). If \(EV(\theta_0)<\infty\) and conditions (5.1.1), (4.1), (A1.1'), and (A7.1)--(A7.7) hold, then \(\theta_n\in Q_{\lambda_0}\) infinitely often almost surely. For every positive integer \(l\), the maximum iterate norm during the excursion between the \(l\)-th and \((l+1)\)-st returns to \(Q_{\lambda_0}\) is bounded in probability. Moreover, \(Q_{\lambda_0}\) may be used as \(R_\rho\) for every \(\rho\in(0,1]\) in Theorem 7.1, and \(\lim_{K\to\infty}\sup_nP\{|\theta_n|\ge K\}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated smooth, radially unbounded Lyapunov function and stochastic-approximation conditions, the iterates return to the Lyapunov sublevel set infinitely often almost surely. Every fixed return-to-return excursion is bounded in probability, that sublevel set satisfies the recurrence requirement with probability one, and the entire iterate sequence is bounded in probability.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ has continuous first and bounded mixed second partial derivatives}

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled-Limit Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Borkar–Meyn-type scaling conditions for stability of stochastic-approximation recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a drift \(h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\), define \(h_c(x)=h(cx)/c\) for \(c\geq1\). The scaled-limit criterion holds if a locally Lipschitz map \(h_\infty\) exists such that \(h_c\to h_\infty\) uniformly on every compact subset of \(\mathbb{R}^d\), and the origin is a globally asymptotically stable equilibrium of \(\dot z=h_\infty(z)\). For a stochastic recursion, this criterion must be paired with standard gain, martingale-noise, and drift-regularity hypotheses before it yields almost-sure iterate boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescale the drift at increasing radii; require compact-uniform convergence to a limiting drift whose ODE has a globally asymptotically stable origin.
assumptions_latex: \(h_c\) converges uniformly on compact sets to a locally Lipschitz \(h_\infty\).
The origin is globally asymptotically stable for \(\dot z=h_\infty(z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((h,h_\infty)\) satisfies the scaled-limit stability criterion.

notation.meaning: drift observed at spatial scale c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the scaled-limit leaf and appropriately avoids claiming boundedness by itself, but the precise scaling convergence and limiting-ODE requirements need an authoritative Borkar–Meyn-type locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Limiting ODE Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global asymptotic stability condition for the ODE governing the drift at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_\infty:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be locally Lipschitz with \(h_\infty(0)=0\), and let \(\phi(t,z_0)\) denote the unique maximal solution of \(\dot z=h_\infty(z)\), \(z(0)=z_0\). The limiting ODE has a globally asymptotically stable origin when every solution exists for all \(t\geq0\), the origin is Lyapunov stable, and \(\lim_{t\to\infty}\phi(t,z_0)=0\) for every \(z_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The limiting ODE is stable when all forward solutions exist, nearby states remain nearby, and every initial state converges to the origin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\) is globally asymptotically stable exactly when it is Lyapunov stable, all forward solutions are global, and \(\phi(t,z_0)\to0\) for every \(z_0\).

notation.meaning: ODE solution at time t from initial state z_0

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global asymptotic stability condition is standard, precise, and appropriate for the leaf, but no authoritative section, definition, theorem, or page locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform contraction of sufficiently scaled flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window scaled-flow consequence of the limiting-ODE stability and approximation hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the standing scaling-limit hypotheses, there exist \(c_0>0\) and \(T>0\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) with \(\|x\|=1\), every \(c>c_0\), and every \(t\in[T,T+1]\), \(\|\phi_c(t,x)\|<1/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the scaling-limit hypotheses, all sufficiently highly scaled flows starting on the unit sphere remain inside the ball of radius one quarter throughout a common unit-length time window.
assumptions_latex: \text{The standing scaling-limit hypotheses, including the limiting-ODE stability condition, hold}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-based theorem transferring the conclusions of Theorems 7.3 and 7.4; the referenced perturbations, bounds, auxiliary sequences, and conclusions are not expanded in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\epsilon_n=\epsilon\) and \(\theta_{n+1}^{\epsilon}=\theta_n^{\epsilon}+\epsilon Y_n^{\epsilon}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Convergence from Recurrence and a Lyapunov-Stable Limiting ODE
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ODE-method convergence theorem for an unconstrained stochastic-approximation recursion with correlated noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume recursion (7.1), conditions (5.1.1), (A.1.1'), (A1.2), (A1.3), (A7.1), and (A1.4')--(A1.7'). Suppose that for every \(\rho\in(0,1)\) there is a compact set \(R_\rho\) such that \(P\{\theta_n\in R_\rho\ \mathrm{i.o.}\}\ge\rho\). Let \(V\in C^1\) satisfy \(V\ge0\), \(V(\theta)\to\infty\) as \(|\theta|\to\infty\), and, for some \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1>0\), \(\dot V(\theta(t))\le-\lambda_1\) whenever \(\dot\theta=\bar g(\theta)\) and \(V(\theta(t))\ge\lambda_0\). Then almost surely \(\theta_n\) approaches the largest bounded invariant set of this ODE contained in \(Q_{\lambda_0}=\{x:V(x)\le\lambda_0\}\). If (A5.2.6) also holds, \(\theta_n\) converges almost surely to a unique \(S_i\). Under the additional hypotheses of Theorem 5.2.5, almost every sample path converges to a set of chain-recurrent points in that invariant set. The same conclusions hold for state-dependent noise under localized versions of the conditions of Theorem 6.1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the cited stochastic-approximation assumptions, compact-set recurrence, and a radially unbounded Lyapunov function that decreases uniformly outside a sublevel set for the limiting ODE, the iterates almost surely approach the largest bounded invariant set within that sublevel set. The stated additional conditions strengthen this to convergence to a unique set or to chain-recurrent points and extend the conclusions to localized state-dependent noise.

children.title: Large-Radius Drift Geometry
children.top_down_role: Directional behavior of the mean field far from bounded regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Large-Radius Drift Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform radial inward drift outside a ball as a large-scale stability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be locally Lipschitz. A quadratic large-radius inward-drift condition holds if constants \(R\geq0\) and \(\mu>0\) satisfy \[\langle x,h(x)\rangle\leq-\mu\lVert x\rVert^2\qquad\text{whenever }\lVert x\rVert\geq R.\] Along any solution of \(\dot z=h(z)\) lying outside the radius-\(R\) ball, \[\frac{d}{dt}\frac12\lVert z(t)\rVert^2\leq-\mu\lVert z(t)\rVert^2.\] Hence the squared radius decreases strictly until the trajectory reaches that ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the drift has a uniformly negative radial component beyond a fixed radius, ODE trajectories contract toward that radius at a quadratic rate.
assumptions_latex: There exist \(R\geq0\) and \(\mu>0\) satisfying the displayed radial inequality.

notation.meaning: radius beyond which inward drift is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The radial drift condition and differential inequality are mathematically coherent and match the leaf, but the record lacks the required inspectable citation.

children.title: Unstable Scaled Limits
children.top_down_role: Large-scale limiting dynamics incompatible with iterate boundedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Scaled Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the large-scale ODE criterion to certify bounded stochastic-approximation iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the recursion \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1})\) and the scaled fields \(h_c(x)=h(cx)/c\). Suppose that, along some sequence \(c_k\to\infty\), the fields \(h_{c_k}\) converge uniformly on compact sets to \(h_\infty\). If the limiting ODE \(\dot x=h_\infty(x)\) has a solution starting on the unit sphere that does not enter any fixed ball \(B_\rho(0)\), with \(0<\rho<1\), within a common finite time, then the usual scaled-ODE contraction argument fails. Consequently, this scaled limit alone supplies no boundedness certificate for \((x_n)\); additional drift, Lyapunov, projection, or coercivity assumptions are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a scaled limiting ODE does not contract unit-scale states toward the origin, the standard large-radius rescaling argument cannot certify bounded stochastic-approximation iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(h_{c_k}\to h_\infty\) uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb R^d\)
\(\exists x_0,\ \lVert x_0\rVert=1\), whose limiting-ODE trajectory lacks the stated uniform contraction
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled-limit stability criterion does not imply \(\sup_n\lVert x_n\rVert<\infty\).

notation.meaning: mean field viewed at spatial scale c
open Euclidean ball of radius rho centered at zero

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between failure of a sufficient scaled-ODE certificate and actual iterate instability is appropriate, but the required uniform trajectory and time quantifiers are unclear and no authoritative scaled-ODE locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robbins–Siegmund Almost-Supermartingale Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventwise convergence and descent summability under a conditional almost-supermartingale inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\mathcal F_n)$ be an increasing sequence of $\sigma$-algebras, and let $V_n,\alpha_n,\beta_n,\gamma_n$ be nonnegative random variables adapted to $\mathcal F_n$. If, for every $n$, $$\mathbb E[V_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]\le (1+\alpha_n)V_n+\beta_n-\gamma_n,$$ then, almost surely on $$A=\left\{\sum_n\alpha_n<\infty,\ \sum_n\beta_n<\infty\right\},$$ the sequence $(V_n)$ converges and $\sum_n\gamma_n<\infty$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative adapted sequences satisfying the conditional almost-supermartingale inequality, the state sequence converges and the accumulated descent terms are finite almost surely on the event where the multiplicative and additive errors are summable.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal F_n)\text{ is an increasing sequence of }\sigma\text{-algebras}

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Supermartingale Arguments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Siegmund convergence principle for nonnegative adapted processes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_n)\) be a filtration. Let \((V_n)\) be a sequence of nonnegative, integrable, \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted random variables, and let \((U_n)\), \((A_n)\), and \((B_n)\) be nonnegative \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted random variables. Assume almost surely that \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}A_n<\infty\), \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}B_n<\infty\), and \[\mathbb E[V_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq (1+A_n)V_n-U_n+B_n\quad\text{for every }n.\] Then \((V_n)\) converges almost surely to a finite random variable and \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}U_n<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integrable nonnegative adapted process, conditional descent with summable multiplicative and additive errors forces convergence to a finite limit and finite accumulated descent almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(V_n\) is nonnegative, integrable, and \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted; \(U_n,A_n,B_n\geq0\) are \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted

notation.meaning: nonnegative integrable Lyapunov or error process

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Quasi-Fejér Arguments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional distance descent relative to a nonempty closed solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonempty closed subset of a Hilbert space \(H\), and let \((x_n)\) be adapted to \((\mathcal F_n)\), with \(\mathbb E\lVert x_n-s\rVert^2<\infty\) for every \(n\) and every fixed \(s\in S\). Suppose that, for every fixed \(s\in S\), there are nonnegative adapted processes \((\alpha_n)\), \((\beta_n(s))\), and \((\delta_n)\) such that \[\mathbb E[\lVert x_{n+1}-s\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq(1+\alpha_n)\lVert x_n-s\rVert^2-\delta_n+\beta_n(s),\] where \(\sum_n\alpha_n<\infty\) and \(\sum_n\beta_n(s)<\infty\) almost surely. Then, for each fixed \(s\in S\), \(\lVert x_n-s\rVert^2\) converges almost surely, and \(\sum_n\delta_n<\infty\) almost surely. Additional limit-set assumptions are required to conclude that \((x_n)\) converges to a point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each fixed target point, a conditional quasi-Fejér inequality makes the squared distance converge almost surely and makes accumulated descent finite; identifying a limit in the target set requires additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(x_n\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted and \(\mathbb E\lVert x_n-s\rVert^2<\infty\) for every \(n\) and fixed \(s\in S\)
For each fixed \(s\in S\), the displayed inequality holds and \(\sum_n\alpha_n<\infty\), \(\sum_n\beta_n(s)<\infty\) almost surely
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each fixed \(s\in S\), \(\lVert x_n-s\rVert^2\) converges almost surely, and \(\sum_n\delta_n<\infty\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: summable additive perturbation for the fixed reference point s

knowledge_statements.title: Accumulated Descent Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summability consequence of a Robbins–Siegmund conditional-descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((V_n)\) be nonnegative, integrable, and adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_n)\), and let \((D_n)\) and \((E_n)\) be nonnegative adapted processes. If \[\mathbb E[V_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq V_n-D_n+E_n\] and \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E_n<\infty\) almost surely, then \[\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}D_n<\infty\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Hence, if \(D_n=a_nr_n\) with \(a_n,r_n\geq0\), then \(\sum_na_nr_n<\infty\) almost surely. This weighted summability alone does not imply \(r_n\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summably perturbed conditional descent inequality for an integrable Lyapunov process makes total descent finite. Weighted residual summability follows, but residual convergence requires additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(V_n\geq0\) is integrable and \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted; \(D_n,E_n\geq0\) are \(\mathcal F_n\)-adapted
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_nD_n<\infty\) almost surely; if \(D_n=a_nr_n\), then \(\sum_na_nr_n<\infty\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Residual Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions converting weighted residual summability into vanishing residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((a_n)\) and \((r_n)\) be nonnegative sequences satisfying \(\sum_na_n=\infty\) and \(\sum_na_nr_n<\infty\). Then \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}r_n=0\). Moreover, assume the following persistence condition: for every \(\varepsilon>0\), if \(r_n\geq2\varepsilon\) for infinitely many \(n\), then there exist \(c_\varepsilon>0\) and infinitely many pairwise disjoint finite integer intervals \(I_j\) such that each \(I_j\) contains an index \(n_j\) with \(r_{n_j}\geq2\varepsilon\), while \(r_k\geq\varepsilon\) for every \(k\in I_j\) and \(\sum_{k\in I_j}a_k\geq c_\varepsilon\). Under this additional condition, \(r_n\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted residual summability with divergent total weight implies zero lower limit. If every recurring residual spike persists over a uniformly positive amount of weight, then the residual converges to zero.
assumptions_latex: The stated positive-weight persistence condition holds when full convergence is asserted

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Limit Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional stochastic quasi-Fejér limit identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty and closed, and let \((x_n)\) be a sequence of \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued random vectors. Suppose there is an event \(\Omega_0\) of probability one such that, for every \(\omega\in\Omega_0\), the sequence \((x_n(\omega))\) is bounded, \(\lVert x_n(\omega)-s\rVert\) converges for every \(s\in S\), and every cluster point of \((x_n(\omega))\) belongs to \(S\). Then there exists an \(S\)-valued random vector \(x_\infty\) such that \(x_n\to x_\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, if boundedness, convergence of all distances to the target, and admissibility of every cluster point hold on one full-probability event, the random sequence converges almost surely to one target point.
assumptions_latex: On one event \(\Omega_0\) with \(\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1\), \((x_n)\) is bounded and \(\lVert x_n-s\rVert\) converges for every \(s\in S\)
On the same event \(\Omega_0\), every cluster point of \((x_n)\) lies in \(S\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an \(S\)-valued random vector \(x_\infty\) such that \(x_n\to x_\infty\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Point Admissibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate placing all finite-dimensional cluster points in the target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)\) be continuous and let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:R(x)=0\}\). If a sequence \((x_n)\subset\mathbb R^d\) satisfies \(R(x_n)\to0\), then every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_n)\) belongs to \(S\). In particular, when \((x_n)\) is bounded, the vanishing residual certifies that all of its nonempty collection of cluster points is admissible. The same statement holds pathwise for a stochastic sequence on any event where residual convergence holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous residual whose zero set is the target certifies that every cluster point is admissible whenever the residual vanishes; boundedness additionally guarantees the existence of cluster points in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) of \((x_n)\) satisfies \(\bar x\in S\); if \((x_n)\) is bounded, at least one such cluster point exists.

knowledge_statements.title: ODE Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic-pseudotrajectory form of the ODE method for bounded stochastic approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+e_n)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\). Assume that \(h\) is locally Lipschitz, \(a_n>0\), \(a_n\to0\), \(\sum_na_n=\infty\), and the iterates are almost surely bounded. If, on every bounded continuous-time window, the accumulated interpolated noise and error vanish asymptotically, then the affine interpolation \(X(t)\), defined at times \(t_n=\sum_{k<n}a_k\), is almost surely an asymptotic pseudotrajectory of the flow generated by \(\dot x=h(x)\). Consequently, its compact limit set is invariant and internally chain transitive for that flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under boundedness and vanishing accumulated perturbations, the interpolated stochastic-approximation path asymptotically follows the mean ODE, and its limit set is invariant and internally chain transitive.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is locally Lipschitz and \((x_n)\) is almost surely bounded
Accumulated \(M_{n+1}+e_n\) vanishes uniformly on each bounded interpolated-time window
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) is an asymptotic pseudotrajectory of \(\dot x=h(x)\), and its limit set is compact, invariant, and internally chain transitive almost surely.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chain Recurrence and Chain Connectedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines arbitrarily accurate pseudo-orbit returns with arbitrarily long solution segments for ordinary and constrained ODEs, and records that invariance alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x(t\mid y)\) denote the relevant solution at time \(t\) from \(y\) of either \(\dot x=\bar g(x)\) or \(\dot x=\bar g(x)+z\), \(z\in-C(x)\). A point \(x\) is chain recurrent if, for every \(\delta>0\) and \(T>0\), there exist \(k\ge0\), points \(u_0,\ldots,u_k\), and times \(T_0,\ldots,T_k\ge T\) such that, with \(y_i=x(T_{i-1}\mid u_{i-1})\) for \(1\le i\le k+1\), \(\|x-u_0\|\le\delta\), \(\|y_i-u_i\|\le\delta\) for \(1\le i\le k\), and \(\|y_{k+1}-x\|\le\delta\). Points \(x\) and \(\bar x\) are chain connected if, for every \(\delta,T>0\), such a chain exists from \(x\) to \(\bar x\) and another exists from \(\bar x\) to \(x\). Membership in a limit set or invariant set does not by itself imply chain recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is chain recurrent when, for every error tolerance and minimum segment duration, a finite pseudo-orbit of sufficiently long solution segments can start near the point and return near it, with every intervening jump within the tolerance. Two points are chain connected when such pseudo-orbits exist in both directions. Membership in a limit or invariant set alone does not guarantee chain recurrence.
assumptions_latex: x(t\mid y)\text{ denotes the relevant solution of }\dot x=\bar g(x)\text{ or }\dot x=\bar g(x)+z,\ z\in-C(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is chain recurrent}\iff\forall\delta,T>0\ \exists k,u_0,\ldots,u_k,T_0,\ldots,T_k\ge T\text{ forming a }(\delta,T)\text{-chain from }x\text{ to }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected ODE on a Hyperrectangle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition, boundary correction, and conditional uniqueness of a projected flow on a hyperrectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^r:a_i\le x_i\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,r\}. Define C(x)=\{0\} for x\in H^0; for x\in\partial H, let C(x) be the convex cone generated by the outward normals of the faces containing x. The projected ODE is \dot x(t)=\bar g(x(t))+z(t), where z(t)\in-C(x(t)) is the minimum correction required to keep x(t)\in H. The correction vanishes in the interior and cancels outward motion at the boundary. It is determined almost everywhere by H and \bar g. If \dot x=\bar g(x) has a unique solution for every initial condition, then the projected ODE also has a unique solution for every initial condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected ODE adds the smallest inward normal-cone correction needed to keep its trajectory in the hyperrectangle. The correction vanishes in the interior and cancels outward boundary motion. Apart from its almost-everywhere definition, it is determined by the set and vector field; uniqueness of the unprojected ODE implies uniqueness of the projected ODE.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute Continuity of the Projected-ODE Constraining Term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded regularity result retaining the source's referenced constraint-set and projected-ODE conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume one of the constraint-set conditions \(\mathrm{(A3.1)}\), \(\mathrm{(A3.2)}\), or \(\mathrm{(A3.3)}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Gronwall Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-interval integral inequality with the source's uniform bound using the terminal-time integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $u,v:[0,T]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and let $C,K,T\ge 0$. If $u(t)\le C+K\int_0^t u(s)v(s)\,ds$ for every $t\in[0,T]$, then $u(t)\le C\exp\!\left(K\int_0^T v(s)\,ds\right)$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral Representation of a Projected ODE
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral formulation of a projected limiting flow and its accumulated constraint correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projected ODE has a Lipschitz trajectory x satisfying x(t)\in H for all t and a process Z with Z(0)=0 such that, for every t and \tau>0, x(t+\tau)=x(t)+\int_t^{t+\tau}\bar g(x(s))\,ds+Z(t+\tau)-Z(t). If x(s)\in H^0 for almost every s\in[t,t+\tau], then Z(t+\tau)-Z(t)=0; in all cases, Z(t+\tau)-Z(t)\in-\operatorname{co}\left(\bigcup_{t\le s\le t+\tau}C(x(s))\right), where \operatorname{co} denotes closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected flow equals the integrated drift plus an accumulated constraint correction. The correction has zero increment when the trajectory lies in the interior almost everywhere, and each increment belongs to the negative closed convex hull of the constraint cones encountered over the interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}x(t+\tau)&=x(t)+\int_t^{t+\tau}\bar g(x(s))\,ds+Z(t+\tau)-Z(t),\\x(s)\in H^0\text{ a.e. on }[t,t+\tau]&\implies Z(t+\tau)-Z(t)=0,\\Z(t+\tau)-Z(t)&\in-\operatorname{co}\left(\bigcup_{t\le s\le t+\tau}C(x(s))\right).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.title: Differential-Inclusion Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued dynamical method for bounded stochastic approximation with nonsmooth mean fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(v_n+M_{n+1}+e_n)\), where \(v_n\in F(x_n)\) and \(F:\mathbb R^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^d\) is a Marchaud map: its values are nonempty, compact, and convex; its graph is closed; and it has linear growth. Assume \(a_n\to0\), \(\sum_na_n=\infty\), the iterates are almost surely bounded, and accumulated perturbations vanish on bounded interpolated-time windows. Then the affine interpolation is almost surely a perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of
\[\dot x(t)\in F(x(t)).\]
Its compact limit set is invariant in the set-valued sense and internally chain transitive for the induced semiflow relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a Marchaud mean-field map and negligible accumulated perturbations, interpolation follows a differential inclusion whose compact limit set is invariant and internally chain transitive.
assumptions_latex: \(a_n>0,\ a_n\to0,\ \sum_na_n=\infty\), and \((x_n)\) is almost surely bounded
Accumulated perturbations vanish on bounded interpolated-time windows
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interpolation asymptotically follows \(\dot x\in F(x)\), and its limit set is compact, invariant, and internally chain transitive almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Limit Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant compact sets for continuous-time limiting dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\times X\to X\) be a continuous semiflow on a metric space \(X\). A nonempty compact set \(L\subset X\) is invariant if
\[\Phi_t(L)=L\quad\text{for every }t\ge0,\]
where \(\Phi_t(x)=\Phi(t,x)\). For a differential inclusion, invariance means that for every \(x\in L\) there exists a complete solution \(z:\mathbb R\to L\) with \(z(0)=x\) that remains in \(L\) for all time. If a precompact trajectory has an omega-limit set and is an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, that omega-limit set is invariant under the corresponding limiting dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant limit set is compact, nonempty, and preserved by the limiting flow; for an inclusion, every point lies on a complete trajectory contained in the set.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is a continuous semiflow on a metric space \(X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is invariant exactly when \(\Phi_t(L)=L\) for every \(t\ge0\), with the stated complete-solution interpretation for inclusions.

notation.meaning: time-t map of the limiting semiflow
complete solution of a differential inclusion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but the record combines strong semiflow invariance, a differential-inclusion complete-solution notion, and an asymptotic-pseudotrajectory theorem. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Time-shifted asynchronous processes and interpolations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines processor-specific sequences and time changes after the first update at or after an arbitrary real time origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\sigma>0\), \(n\geq0\), and \(\alpha\leq r\), let \(p_\alpha^\epsilon(\sigma)\) index the first update of processor \(\alpha\) at or after time \(\sigma\), and define \(\theta_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}=\theta_{p_\alpha^\epsilon(\sigma)+n,\alpha}^{\epsilon}\), \(Y_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}=Y_{p_\alpha^\epsilon(\sigma)+n,\alpha}^{\epsilon}\), \(E_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}=E_{p_\alpha^\epsilon(\sigma)+n,\alpha}^{\epsilon}\), and \(E_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma,+}=E_{p_\alpha^\epsilon(\sigma)+n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,+}\); shift \(\delta\tau,\beta,\Delta,\Delta^+,\xi,\psi,g\), and \(u\) analogously. Set \(\tau_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}=\epsilon\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\delta\tau_{i,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}\). For \(t\geq0\), define \(\theta_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma}(t)=\theta_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}\) and \(\tau_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma}(t)=\tau_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}\) on \([n\epsilon,n\epsilon+\epsilon)\), while \(\widehat\theta_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma}(t)=\theta_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma}\) and \(N_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma}(t)=n\epsilon\) on \([\tau_{n,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma},\tau_{n+1,\alpha}^{\epsilon,\sigma})\). Consequently, \(N_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma}(\tau_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma}(t))=n\epsilon\) for \(t\in[n\epsilon,n\epsilon+\epsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After translating the time origin to an arbitrary real time σ, each processor's sequences are reindexed from its first update at or after σ. The cumulative local time is the scaled sum of update-time increments. Piecewise-constant interpolations are then defined on algorithmic-time and local-time intervals, with the local-time inverse satisfying the stated composition identity.
assumptions_latex: p_\alpha^\epsilon(\sigma)\text{ indexes the first update of processor }\alpha\text{ at or after real time }\sigma

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Weighted Averages to a Single Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An Opial-type finite-dimensional criterion for convergence of weighted averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), let \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\), and define \(\bar x^k=\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^k\alpha_i x^i\bigr)/\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^k\alpha_i\bigr)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tightness and limit-set tracking for shifted asynchronous stochastic approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded theorem whose main ownership is stochastic-approximation invariant-limit-set analysis; its detailed hypotheses and limiting equations are inherited from Theorem 3.3 and the cited equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the conditions of Theorem 3.3 with superscript \((\epsilon,\sigma)\). Then the family \(\{(\theta_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma},\tau_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma},\widehat\theta_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma},N_\alpha^{\epsilon,\sigma});\ \alpha\le r,\epsilon,\sigma\}\) is tight in \(D^{4r}[0,\infty)\). Along any weakly convergent subsequence as \(\epsilon\to0\) and \(\sigma\to\infty\), the limit satisfies (3.12)--(3.16), and \(\widehat\theta(\cdot)\in L_H\) almost surely. For every bounded continuous \(F\) on \(D^r(-\infty,\infty)\), \(\mathbb E F(\widehat\theta^{\epsilon,\sigma}(\epsilon q_\epsilon+\cdot))\to\mathbb E F(\widehat\theta(\cdot))\). There exist \(T_{\epsilon,\sigma}\to\infty\) such that \(\limsup_{\epsilon}P\{\widehat\theta^{\epsilon,\sigma}(t)\notin N_\delta(L_H)\text{ for some }t\le T_{\epsilon,\sigma}\}=0\). If \(A\) is the set of chain-recurrent points in the limit or invariant set, \(\epsilon q_\epsilon\to\infty\), and the solution of (3.15) or (3.16) is unique for each initial condition, then \(A\) may replace \(L_H\). If the constraint set \(H\) is removed and \(\{\widehat\theta_n^{\epsilon,\sigma};\epsilon,\sigma,n\}\) is tight, the conclusions hold with \(\widehat z(t)=0\) and a bounded invariant set of the ODE replacing \(L_H\). For the differential-inclusion case, if \(U_\alpha\) is upper semicontinuous and condition (3.25) holds, the assertions hold with the dynamics specified by (3.21)--(3.22).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the shifted hypotheses of Theorem 3.3, the asynchronous stochastic-approximation interpolations form a tight family. Joint small-step and late-start weak limits satisfy the cited limiting dynamics and lie almost surely in the constrained limit set. Shifted path functionals converge, and with high probability the process remains near that set over horizons tending to infinity. Under the stated additional assumptions, the conclusion sharpens to the chain-recurrent set and extends to unconstrained dynamics and differential inclusions.

\text{For replacement by }A:\quad \epsilon q_\epsilon\to\infty\text{ and the solution of (3.15) or (3.16) is unique for every initial condition}.
\text{For the unconstrained variant: }H\text{ is removed and }\{\widehat\theta_n^{\epsilon,\sigma};\epsilon,\sigma,n\}\text{ is tight}.
\text{For the differential-inclusion variant: }U_\alpha\text{ is upper semicontinuous and condition (3.25) holds}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chain-recurrence refinement of projected-ODE limit sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that accumulation points recurrently approached by the iterates are chain connected and sharpens invariant- or limit-set convergence to chain-recurrent points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant sets and forward limit sets of autonomous ODEs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential invariance, omega-limit sets, and the compact-invariance property of bounded autonomous trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the autonomous ODE \(\dot x=\bar g(x)\), a set \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^r\) is invariant in the source's existential sense if, for every \(x_0\in\Lambda\), there exists a complete solution \(x:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^r\) satisfying \(x(0)=x_0\) and \(x(t)\in\Lambda\) for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\). The forward limit set of a trajectory is \[\omega(x_0)=\bigcap_{t\ge0}\overline{\{x(s):s\ge t\}}.\] If the trajectory is bounded, then its forward limit set is compact and invariant. It need not be a singleton; a non-equilibrium harmonic-oscillator trajectory has a periodic-orbit limit set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant set contains at least one complete trajectory through each of its points. A forward limit set contains the accumulation points of a trajectory at times tending to infinity. For a bounded trajectory of an autonomous ODE, this set is compact and invariant, but it may be a periodic orbit rather than one point.
assumptions_latex: \text{For compactness and invariance of }\omega(x_0),\ \{x(t):t\ge0\}\text{ is bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Lambda\text{ is invariant in the stated sense if }\forall x_0\in\Lambda\ \exists x:\mathbb{R}\to\Lambda\text{ solving the ODE with }x(0)=x_0;\quad \omega(x_0)=\bigcap_{t\ge0}\overline{\{x(s):s\ge t\}}\text{ is compact and invariant for a bounded trajectory and need not be a singleton}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak ODE-limit theorem for unconstrained stochastic approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded weak-convergence theorem identifying subsequential limits and invariant ODE sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the step-size condition (5.1.1), uniform integrability of \(\{Y_n\}\), absence of the constraint set \(H\), and boundedness in probability of \(\{\theta_n\}\). Suppose \(E_nY_n=\bar g(\theta_n)+\beta_n\), where \(E|\beta_n|\to0\) and \(\bar g\) is bounded and continuous. Assume that, from every initial condition, the ODE \(\dot\theta=\bar g(\theta)\) has a unique solution in either time direction and that its limit set \(L\), over all initial conditions, is bounded. Every subsequence of \(\{\widetilde\theta^n\}\) then has a further subsequence \(\{\widetilde\theta^{n_k}\}\) converging in distribution on \(C^r[0,\infty)\) to an ODE solution \(\theta\): for every bounded continuous real-valued \(F\), \(EF(\widetilde\theta^{n_k})\to EF(\theta)\). Almost surely, the limit process takes values in an invariant set of the ODE, and conclusion (2.4b) holds with that invariant set in place of \(L_H\). If \(L=\{\bar\theta\}\), the full sequence converges weakly to the constant path \(t\mapsto\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unconstrained stochastic approximation with uniformly integrable noise, bounded-in-probability iterates, vanishing conditional-mean error, and a bounded continuous mean field whose ODE is uniquely solvable in either time direction and has a bounded limit set, every interpolated-process subsequence has a further weakly convergent subsequence. Its limit solves the mean ODE and lies almost surely in an invariant ODE set. The increasing-horizon proximity conclusion also holds for that set; a singleton limit set gives full-sequence weak convergence to the corresponding constant path.

\{Y_n\}\text{ is uniformly integrable, and }\{\theta_n\}\text{ is bounded in probability.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and limit-point geometry of stochastic quasi-Fejér sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of the stochastic quasi-Fejér property relative to W; the theorem does not assert that all limit points belong to W.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\{\mathbf w^v\}\) is stochastic quasi-Fejér with respect to \(W\), then for every \(w\in W\), \(\|w-\mathbf w^{v+1}\|^2\) converges almost surely and the distances have a finite uniform expectation bound. Almost surely, \(\{\mathbf w^v(\omega)\}\) has at least one limit point. Moreover, if two distinct limit points \(\bar w^1(\omega),\bar w^2(\omega)\notin W\) exist, then there is a hyperplane \(\eta=\{w:\alpha^Tw=\alpha_0\}\) with \(W\subseteq\eta\) such that \[\|\bar w^1-\Pi_\eta(\bar w^1)\|=\|\bar w^2-\Pi_\eta(\bar w^2)\|.\]

If it has two distinct limit points outside W, then W lies in a hyperplane from which those two points are equally distant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant and internally chain-transitive sets of an ODE flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flow-based invariance and internal-chain definitions for closed subsets of the ODE state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ be closed. It is invariant (respectively positively or negatively invariant) if every trajectory with $x(0)\in A$ remains in $A$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$ (respectively all $t\ge 0$ or all $t\le 0$). An invariant set is internally chain transitive if it is compact and, for every $x,y\in A$ and every $\epsilon,T>0$, there exist $n\ge 1$ and $x_0,\ldots,x_n\in A$ with $x_n=y$ and $\|x_0-x\|<\epsilon$ such that, for each $0\le i<n$, the trajectory initiated at $x_i$ enters the $\epsilon$-neighborhood of $x_{i+1}$ after a time at least $T$. Restricting this chain condition to $y=x$ defines internal chain recurrence. If the ODE has unique global forward and backward solutions, its solution maps $\{\Phi_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ form a group of homeomorphisms, and $A$ is invariant exactly when $\Phi_t(A)=A$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; positive and negative invariance correspond to $\Phi_t(A)\subseteq A$ for $t\ge0$ and $t\le0$, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed set is invariant when every trajectory starting in it stays there for all time, with forward- and backward-time variants. A compact invariant set is internally chain transitive when any two points can be connected by arbitrarily accurate trajectory chains whose segments last at least a prescribed time; return chains define internal chain recurrence. Under unique global two-sided solutions, invariance is equivalently expressed through the ODE flow maps.

children.title: Attractor Limit Sets
children.top_down_role: Stable limiting regions that capture nearby trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Attractor Limit Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact invariant sets that uniformly attract a neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) be a continuous semiflow on a metric space \((X,d)\). A nonempty compact invariant set \(A\subset X\) is an attractor if there exists an open neighborhood \(U\supset A\) such that
\[\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in U} d(\Phi_t(x),A)=0,\qquad d(y,A)=\inf_{a\in A}d(y,a).\]
The basin of attraction is
\[B(A)=\{x\in X:d(\Phi_t(x),A)\to0\text{ as }t\to\infty\}.\]
A trajectory whose tail eventually remains in a compact subset of \(B(A)\) has omega-limit set contained in \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attractor is a compact invariant set uniformly approached from some neighborhood; trajectories eventually confined within its basin have limit sets contained in the attractor.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is a continuous semiflow on the metric space \((X,d)\)
\(A\subset X\) is nonempty, compact, and invariant
An open neighborhood \(U\supset A\) satisfies the displayed uniform-attraction condition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is an attractor with basin \(B(A)\); compactly basin-confined trajectory tails have omega-limit sets contained in \(A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but uniform attraction of an entire open neighborhood is stronger than some standard attractor definitions, and the additional omega-limit assertion needs its own hypotheses. A specific dynamical-systems source is required.

children.title: Chain-Transitive Limits
children.top_down_role: Limit sets characterized through approximate dynamical reachability.

knowledge_statements.title: Chain-Transitive Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Internal chain transitivity for compact invariant limit sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) be a continuous semiflow on a metric space \((X,d)\), and let \(L\subset X\) be nonempty and compact. For \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(T>0\), an \((\varepsilon,T)\)-chain in \(L\) from \(x\) to \(y\) consists of points \(x=x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_m=y\) in \(L\) and times \(t_i\ge T\) such that
\[d(\Phi_{t_i}(x_i),x_{i+1})<\varepsilon\quad\text{for }i=0,\ldots,m-1.\]
The set \(L\) is internally chain transitive if such a chain exists for every \(x,y\in L\) and every \(\varepsilon,T>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact set is internally chain transitive when any two of its points can be connected inside it by arbitrarily accurate pseudo-orbit segments of arbitrarily long minimum duration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is internally chain transitive exactly when the displayed chain condition holds for all \(x,y\in L\) and all \(\varepsilon,T>0\).

notation.meaning: jump tolerance and minimum flow-segment duration
compact set within which every chain remains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chain condition is standard for a semiflow and the definition role fits the leaf, but the scope calls for compact invariant limit sets while invariance is absent from the defining assumptions. A source is also needed to determine whether the intended container includes the relation-based differential-inclusion variant.

children.title: Nonattracting Limit Behavior

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattracting Limit Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a compact invariant limit set that can occur without attracting any full neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \Phi_t:X\to X be a continuous semiflow on a metric space \(X,d)\, and let \(L\subset X\ be nonempty, compact, and invariant. Its basin is \[\mathcal B(L)=\{x\in X:\operatorname{dist}(\Phi_t(x),L)\to0\text{ as }t\to\infty\}.\] The set \(L\ has nonattracting limit behavior when it is the \(\omega\-limit set of at least one trajectory but no open neighborhood of \(L\ is contained in \(\mathcal B(L)\. Thus convergence to \(L\ may occur from exceptional initial conditions without local attraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonattracting invariant set can be a trajectory’s limit set, yet every neighborhood contains initial states whose trajectories do not approach it.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ is a metric space and \(\Phi\ is a continuous semiflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\omega(x)\ for some \(x\in X\, while \(L\ has no neighborhood contained in \(\mathcal B(L)\.

notation.meaning: omega-limit set of the trajectory starting from x

knowledge_statements.title: Lock-In Probability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional probability that stochastic approximation remains in an attracting basin and converges to its attractor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an adapted stochastic-approximation sequence \((x_n)\, an attractor \(A\ of the limiting flow, and an open set \(U\ with \(\overline U\subset\mathcal B(A)\, define the lock-in probability at time \(n\ by \[p_n(U,A)=\mathbb P\!\left(x_k\in\mathcal B(A)\text{ for every }k\ge n,\ \operatorname{dist}(x_k,A)\to0\mid\mathcal F_n,\ x_n\in U\right),\] whenever the conditioning event has positive probability. It quantifies basin retention and convergence after the iterate has entered a prescribed interior neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lock-in probability is the conditional chance that, after entering an interior basin neighborhood, all later iterates remain in the basin and converge to its attractor.

children.title: Attraction-Basin Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structure governing deterministic attraction toward competing limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Attraction-Basin Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basin, boundary, and forward-invariance geometry for an attractor of the limiting flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi_t\ be a continuous semiflow on a metric space \(X\ and let \(A\subset X\ be compact and invariant. Its basin of attraction is \[\mathcal B(A)=\{x\in X:\operatorname{dist}(\Phi_t(x),A)\to0\text{ as }t\to\infty\}.\] If \(A\ is an attractor, then \(\mathcal B(A)\ is open and forward invariant: \(\Phi_t(\mathcal B(A))\subseteq\mathcal B(A)\ for every \(t\ge0\. Its boundary \(\partial\mathcal B(A)\ separates initial states selected by this attractor from states not converging to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attractor’s basin is the open, forward-invariant set of initial states converging to it; its boundary separates distinct asymptotic selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B(A)\ is open and satisfies \(\Phi_t(\mathcal B(A))\subseteq\mathcal B(A)\ for all \(t\ge0\.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses attractors and basin geometry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the geometry leaf, but openness of the stated convergence basin depends on the precise definition of attractor, which is not supplied. The claim that the boundary separates selections by distinct attractors is stronger than the formal assumptions, since points outside this basin need not converge to another attractor. A cited attractor definition is required, and the TeX delimiters are malformed.

children.title: Initialization Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of attractor selection on starting location.

knowledge_statements.title: Initialization Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates asymptotic attractor selection to the basin containing the initial state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\ be attractors of a limiting semiflow with pairwise disjoint basins \(\mathcal B_i\, and let \(x^\varepsilon\ be stochastic approximations whose perturbation level tends to zero. For every compact \(K\subset\mathcal B_i\ lying a positive distance from \(\partial\mathcal B_i\, basin consistency means \[\inf_{x_0^\varepsilon\in K}\mathbb P\!\left(\operatorname{dist}(x_n^\varepsilon,A_i)\to0\right)\longrightarrow1\quad\text{as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.\] Consequently, initializations in different basin interiors can select different limiting attractors, while initialization near a basin boundary need not have a stable selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under vanishing perturbations, initialization inside a basin selects its attractor with high probability; near basin boundaries, small initialization changes may alter the limit.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathcal B_i\ is compact with positive distance from the basin boundary.
review_flags: The precise basin-consistency hypotheses depend on the stochastic-approximation model.
No matching source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the container, but basin membership and vanishing perturbation alone do not imply the displayed uniform convergence probability. The recursion, time horizon, noise scaling, stability or tracking assumptions, and meaning of convergence as \(n\to\infty\) must be specified by a source. The statement also contains unclosed math delimiters.

children.title: Noise-Driven Basin Escape
children.top_down_role: Departure from attraction basins under persistent stochastic fluctuations.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Driven Basin Escape
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A constant-step stochastic recursion can escape every bounded deterministic attraction neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\alpha<1\ and let \((\xi_n)\ be independent standard Gaussian variables. The recursion \[x_{n+1}=(1-\alpha)x_n+\alpha\xi_{n+1}\] is a noisy discretization of the stable flow \(\dot x=-x\, whose attractor is \(\{0\}\. For every \(R>0\ and every initial value \(x_0\in[-R,R]\, \[\mathbb P\!\left(\sup_{n\ge0}|x_n|>R\right)=1.\] Hence nonvanishing unbounded noise prevents permanent lock-in to any bounded neighborhood, despite deterministic asymptotic stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With constant step size and Gaussian noise, a recursion around a stable equilibrium eventually exits every bounded neighborhood almost surely.

notation.meaning: radius of the proposed lock-in neighborhood

review_flags: Concrete claim is standard for an irreducible stationary Gaussian AR(1) chain, but no supporting locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind is appropriate and the Gaussian AR(1) escape claim is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the almost-sure statement. Because this is a nontrivial recurrence claim rather than a definition, a specific locator is required. The statement also has pervasive delimiter errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Limits of Interpolated Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ODE-method weak-limit theorem for time-shifted, piecewise-linear stochastic-approximation interpolations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+r_n)\ in \(\mathbb R^d\, and form the piecewise-linear interpolation \(\bar x\ on times \(t_n=\sum_{k<n}a_k\. If \(h\ is locally Lipschitz, the iterates are almost surely bounded, \(a_n\downarrow0\ with \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\ and \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\, the martingale noise has uniformly bounded conditional second moments, and \(r_n\to0\, then every weak subsequential limit of \(\bar x(t_n+\cdot)\ is supported on solutions of \(\dot x=h(x)\.

knowledge_statements.title: Diffusion Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Ornstein–Uhlenbeck approximation for constant-step stochastic approximation near a stable equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{n+1}^{\eta}=x_n^{\eta}+\eta(h(x_n^{\eta})+\xi_{n+1})\, where \(h(x_\star)=0\ and \(H=Dh(x_\star)\ is Hurwitz. Suppose the conditional covariance of the martingale-difference noise converges locally to \(Q\ and a functional central-limit condition holds. For \(Z^{\eta}(t)=\eta^{-1/2}(x_{\lfloor t/\eta\rfloor}^{\eta}-x_\star)\, suitably interpolated and initialized with a weakly convergent scaled error, \[Z^{\eta}\Rightarrow Z,\qquad dZ_t=HZ_t\,dt+Q^{1/2}dW_t.\] The stationary covariance \(P\ of the limit satisfies \(HP+PH^{\mathsf T}+Q=0\.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After scaling fluctuations by the square root of the step size, constant-step iterates near a stable equilibrium converge weakly to an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck diffusion.
assumptions_latex: \(h\ is differentiable near \(x_\star\ and \(Dh(x_\star)\ is Hurwitz.
Noise is martingale-difference with local covariance limit \(Q\.
A functional central-limit and scaled-initialization condition holds.
review_flags: No diffusion-approximation source locator was supplied.
Precise tightness and functional central-limit hypotheses require certification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the diffusion-approximation leaf, but the functional central-limit condition, interpolation, path-space topology, localization near the equilibrium, and noise covariance assumptions are only named rather than stated. Those details determine whether the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck conclusion is valid. No supporting locator is supplied, and the statement has malformed delimiters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Convergence and Oracle Complexity of M-SGS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded guarantee under the M-SGS problem and oracle setup associated with (8.1.1).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the M-SGS algorithm uses \(N_0=\left\lceil 2\sqrt{5L/\mu}\right\rceil\), then, for every \(s\ge 0\), \[\mathbb{E}[\Psi(y_s)-\Psi^*]\leq \frac{\Delta_0}{2^s}.\] Consequently, the respective numbers of \(\nabla f\) and \(H\) evaluations required to find a stochastic \(\varepsilon\)-solution are \[\mathcal{O}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu}}\log_2\max\left\{\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon},1\right\}\right)\] and \[\mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{M^2+\sigma^2}{\mu\varepsilon}+\sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu}}\log_2\max\left\{\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon},1\right\}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If M-SGS uses N₀ equal to the ceiling of 2√(5L/μ), its expected objective gap after stage s is at most Δ₀/2ˢ for every s ≥ 0. The stated gradient- and H-oracle complexities then suffice for a stochastic ε-solution.
assumptions_latex: \text{The M-SGS problem and oracle hypotheses associated with (8.1.1) hold.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb{E}[\Psi(y_s)-\Psi^*]\leq \Delta_0/2^s\text{, with the stated respective }\nabla f\text{- and }H\text{-evaluation bounds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Importance-Sampled RPDG Rates and Iteration Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear expected convergence and explicit stochastic-solution complexity under smoothness-weighted component sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i=\frac1{2m}+\frac{L_i}{2mL}\), \(C=8L/\mu\), and use constant RPDG parameters \[\tau=\frac{\sqrt{(m-1)^2+4mC}-(m-1)}{2m},\quad \eta=\frac{\mu\sqrt{(m-1)^2+4mC+\mu(m-1)}}2,\quad \alpha=1-\frac1{(m+1)+\sqrt{(m-1)^2+4mC}}.\] Then, for every \(k\ge1\), \[\mathbb EV(x^k,x^*)\le\left(1+\frac{3L_f}{\mu}\right)\alpha^kV(x^0,x^*),\] \[\mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x^k)-\Psi^*]\le\alpha^{k/2}(1-\alpha)^{-1}\left(\mu+2L_f+\frac{L_f^2}{\mu}\right)V(x^0,x^*).\] Distance-error iteration counts are bounded by \(K(\varepsilon,C)\) and \(K(\lambda\varepsilon,C)\), where \[K(\varepsilon,C)=\left[(m+1)+\sqrt{(m-1)^2+4mC}\right]\log\left[\left(1+\frac{3L_f}{\mu}\right)\frac{V(x^0,x^*)}{\varepsilon}\right].\] Objective-gap iteration counts are bounded by \(\widetilde K(\varepsilon,C)\) and \(\widetilde K(\lambda\varepsilon,C)\), where \[\widetilde K(\varepsilon,C)=2\left[(m+1)+\sqrt{(m-1)^2+4mC}\right]\log\left[2\left(\mu+2L_f+\frac{L_f^2}{\mu}\right)(m+\sqrt{mC})\frac{V(x^0,x^*)}{\varepsilon}\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With component probabilities proportional to a mixture of uniform mass and component smoothness, the specified constant RPDG parameters yield geometric expected distance and objective-gap convergence, together with explicit logarithmic iteration bounds for stochastic epsilon and epsilon-lambda solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb EV(x^k,x^*)\le(1+3L_f/\mu)\alpha^kV(x^0,x^*),\quad \mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x^k)-\Psi^*]\le\alpha^{k/2}(1-\alpha)^{-1}(\mu+2L_f+L_f^2/\mu)V(x^0,x^*),\text{ with the stated }K\text{ and }\widetilde K\text{ iteration bounds}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Step SPS Error Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise potential inequality for the stochastic proximal-sliding inner procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that \(\{p_t\}\) and \(\{\theta_t\}\) satisfy (8.1.20). Then, for every \(t\ge1\) and \(u\in X\),
\[
\frac{\beta}{1-P_t}V(u_t,u)+\Phi(\widetilde u_t)-\Phi(u)
\le \frac{\beta P_t}{1-P_t}V(u_{t-1},u)
+\frac{P_t}{1-P_t}\sum_{i=1}^t\frac{1}{p_iP_{i-1}}
\left[\frac{(M+\|\delta_i\|_*)^2}{2\beta p_i}+\langle\delta_i,u-u_{i-1}\rangle\right],
\]
where \(\Phi\) is defined by (8.1.19) and
\[
\delta_i:=H(u_{i-1},\xi_{i-1})-h'(u_{i-1}),\qquad h'(u_{i-1})=\mathbb E[H(u_{i-1},\xi_{i-1})].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the prescribed SPS parameter relation, each inner iteration bounds its Bregman potential and composite objective gap by the preceding distance and accumulated stochastic-oracle errors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tuned SGS Expected and Concentration Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit objective-gap bounds for two prescribed SGS parameter schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_t,\theta_t\) be set by (8.1.39), and assume (8.1.6) and (8.1.7).

If \(N\) is fixed a priori, \(\beta_k,\gamma_k\) follow (8.1.40), and
\[
T_k=\left\lceil\frac{N(M^2+\sigma^2)k^2}{\widetilde D L^2}\right\rceil,
\]
then
\[
\mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le\frac{2L}{N(N+1)}\left[3V(x_0,x^*)+4\widetilde D\right].
\]
If additionally \(X\) is compact and (8.1.57) holds, the deviation threshold and probability are exactly those displayed in (8.1.74).

If instead \(X\) is compact, \(\beta_k,\gamma_k\) follow (8.1.42), and
\[
T_k=\left\lceil\frac{(M^2+\sigma^2)(k+1)^3}{\widetilde D L^2}\right\rceil,
\]
then
\[
\mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le\frac{L}{(N+1)(N+2)}\left[\frac{27}{2}\bar V(x^*)+\frac{16}{3}\widetilde D\right].
\]
Under (8.1.57), the deviation threshold and probability are exactly those displayed in (8.1.77). In both cases the tail probability is at most \(e^{-2\lambda^2/3}+e^{-\lambda}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two specified SGS schedules give explicit order-1/N-squared expected objective-gap bounds. With compactness and the stated tail assumption, they also give the displayed exponential deviation bounds.
assumptions_latex: \text{Schedule (a): }N\text{ is fixed a priori and }\beta_k,\gamma_k\text{ follow (8.1.40)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le\frac{2L[3V(x_0,x^*)+4\widetilde D]}{N(N+1)}\quad\text{or}\quad\mathbb E[\Psi(\bar x_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le\frac{L[27\bar V(x^*)/2+16\widetilde D/3]}{(N+1)(N+2)},\quad \Pr(\text{displayed deviation event})\le e^{-2\lambda^2/3}+e^{-\lambda}
